gates.title: Foundation
gates.done_when: CI is green, branch protection is on, docker compose up shows the board and a no-op job completes.

gates.title: Spec and render
gates.done_when: make demo-render turns the sample spec into a correct 45 second video inside the worker image.

gates.title: Pipeline and planning
gates.done_when: In demo mode an idea reaches the plan gate, is edited, approved and rendered through the interface.

gates.title: Assets and clips
gates.done_when: A live episode on the owner's PC passes the asset gate with generated images and at least three Wan 2.2 clips.

gates.title: QC and export
gates.done_when: The Render tab shows a QC report and the export zip opens with all five items.

gates.title: Videos and revision loop
gates.done_when: A video is adjusted once and remade once from the Videos screen, all three versions are playable, and Finish writes the export folder.

gates.title: Critic agent
gates.done_when: In demo mode a video with planted defects is auto-fixed, both versions are visible, and every guardrail test passes.

gates.title: Producer agent
gates.done_when: In demo mode an idea reaches the review gate on autopilot, and the producer cannot pass the final review or a rights flag.

gates.title: Showcase
gates.done_when: A stranger can run the demo from the README in under 10 minutes.

gates.title: Tracker published
gates.done_when: This page is published on the owner's hosting. Until then it is served locally only.

phases.title: Create the GitHub repository and open the stacked pull requests
phases.note: The public repository nermo-m/video-factory holds every finished card as one squashed pull request (#1 to #21), CI is green on main and main is protected.

phases.title: Repository skeleton and tooling
phases.note: Verified on a fresh clone. Merged in pull request #1.

phases.title: Progress tracker: page, JSON twin and local server
phases.note: Tests pass, page checked at desktop and phone width. Merged in pull request #2.

phases.title: Docker Compose with web, api, worker and db
phases.note: All four services healthy on this PC, ports on 127.0.0.1 only. Merged in pull request #3.

phases.title: Database models and Alembic baseline
phases.note: 15 tables, baseline migration, 16 integration tests on real Postgres. Merged in pull request #4.

phases.title: Job queue and worker loops
phases.note: Queue and worker verified on real Postgres and in Compose, including worker and database restarts. Merged in pull request #5.

phases.title: API skeleton, health endpoint and generated client
phases.note: Health, common error shape, OpenAPI file and generated client with drift checks. Merged in pull request #6.

phases.title: Web app shell with responsive navigation
phases.note: Shell, status strip and empty Board follow the mockups. 28 browser tests pass, axe clean, screenshots approved at 390, 820 and 1440 px. Merged in pull request #7.

phases.title: CI workflow with all required jobs
phases.note: CI ran on GitHub for the first time on its own pull request and all 12 checks passed. Merged in pull request #8.

phases.title: CD workflows, Dependabot and branch protection
phases.note: On main the release workflow published the web, api and worker images to the GitHub Container Registry. Branch protection, squash-only merging, secret scanning and push protection are on. Merged in pull request #9.

phases.title: Architecture document and ADRs 1 to 5
phases.note: Architecture document with three diagrams and ADRs 1 to 6, kept honest by tests. Merged in pull request #10.

phases.title: JSON Schemas for all pipeline documents
phases.note: Six schemas with 11 valid and 77 invalid fixtures, each failing where it says. Merged in pull request #11.

phases.title: Resolver: cues to absolute times
phases.note: All four cue types, pads, outro hold, the 2 second tolerance and reference checks, 29 tests. Merged in pull request #12.

phases.title: Theme night_scrolls with original assets
phases.note: Original artwork and sounds made by a script, three OFL fonts, capabilities and layout. The asset rebuild test moved here from VFS-13 to meet the coverage gate (92 percent). Merged in pull request #13.

phases.title: Compositor and animation primitives
phases.note: Frame drawing for all five scene kinds and every primitive, deterministic from the seed. 14 golden frames pass inside the worker image. Merged in pull request #14.

phases.title: Kokoro voice adapter with pronunciation and word timings
phases.note: Kokoro voice on ONNX Runtime with espeak-ng as a separate program, pronunciation dictionary, word timings from measured pauses, bundled-sample twin, make models. 92 unit tests and 5 tests on the real model. Merged in pull request #15.

phases.title: Audio mix: cues, music bed, ducking, loudness
phases.note: Narration, sound cues and a synthesised music bed mixed to 48 kHz stereo: voice 13 dB over the music, -14 LUFS, true peak under -1 dB, confirmed by FFmpeg's meter. 56 unit tests and 5 FFmpeg tests. Merged in pull request #16.

phases.title: Scene encode, join, contact sheet and preview mode
phases.note: One H.264 file per scene, joined by copying with AAC sound and faststart. Only changed scenes are encoded again, files appear only when complete, preview mode, clip decoding and the contact sheet. 22 unit tests and 17 FFmpeg tests. Merged in pull request #17.

phases.title: Original sample episode and make demo-render
phases.note: The Lighthouse Keeper: original spec, four pictures drawn in code, narration recorded with the Kokoro voice. make demo-render produces a 44 second video in the worker image and checks its format. Rendered in 53 seconds with 4 workers. Merged in pull request #18.

phases.title: Pipeline state machine, gates and stale marking
phases.note: The episode state machine: jobs per state, three gates, reject with a comment, re-run with stale marking, and stale scenes after a spec edit. The worker moves an episode on in the transaction that stores a job's result. 45 unit and 40 integration tests. Merged in pull request #19.

phases.title: Provider mode switch and paid API guard
phases.note: Paid APIs need the mode and the owner's switch together, and a paid adapter cannot even be built without both. Source scans prove nothing can change the mode, and the database ties the billing type to the provider. 48 unit and 31 integration tests. Merged in pull request #20.

phases.title: LLM adapter with mock and recorded responses
phases.note: The language model adapter: recorded responses for demo mode, the Anthropic adapter with web search behind the paid API guard, and model call logging. Tested through the real SDK with a mock transport, no paid call. 49 unit and 8 integration tests. Merged in pull request #21.

phases.title: Live check of the Anthropic adapter against the real API
phases.note: Needs owner: an API key, PROVIDER_MODE=api with the Use paid APIs switch on, and a development budget of about 1 US dollar.

phases.title: Host CLI bridge for Claude Code and Codex
phases.note: The host bridge for subscription mode: /health, /claude and /codex on 127.0.0.1:8189, plan sign-in checked before every call, key variables removed, usage limits mapped to plan_limit, web pages refused. Every flag confirmed against the installed tools without a model call (ADR 8). 277 unit tests with fake tools. Merged in pull request #27.

phases.title: Live check of the host bridge with the signed-in tools
phases.note: Nine short live calls on the owner's plans, with his go-ahead. Everything held. The bridge now reads Claude Code's streaming output: the session's model, the pages a search retrieved, and the tool's own usage report (ADR 9). Captured outputs are test fixtures. Merged in pull request #30.

phases.title: Claude CLI and Codex CLI adapters
phases.note: The adapters of subscription mode: ClaudeCliLLM and CodexCliLLM call the host bridge, a plan call costs nothing, a usage limit makes the job wait until the reset time, and neither adapter can be built in another mode. 57 unit tests through a real bridge with fake tools. Merged in pull request #28.

phases.title: Usage and limits tracker with owner budgets
phases.note: The usage and limits tracker: 5 hour and 7 day counts, budgets that warn at 80 percent and pause at 100, Continue anyway for one episode, limit events with reset time, the automatic and on-demand check, and the four /providers routes. A waiting job stays queued with its reason. Merged in pull request #29.

phases.title: Planner service and skills: brief, research, script
phases.note: The planner service with one corrective retry, and the skills brief, research and script with schemas, examples, tests and demo recordings. A claim without a retrieved source is dropped, and a script must fit its word budget. Worker handlers for the three planning jobs. Merged in pull request #31.

phases.title: Skills: direct, assets, package, revise
phases.note: The skills direct, assets, package and revise, with schemas, examples, tests and demo recordings. A spec may only use what the theme declares and keeps the script's words. The direction is stored as a spec version. A revision is a checked JSON Patch. All seven skills ran live in a row. Merged in pull request #32.

phases.title: Planner skills pass their recorded tests through the bridge
Research sources in subscription mode
phases.note: Research answers in subscription mode carry the pages the tool retrieved. Built together with VFS-65, in pull request #30.

phases.title: Episode API: lifecycle, spec versions and diff
phases.note: The episode routes: list and create, read, advance, approve, reject, rerun, spec read and replace, versions, diff, revise and apply. Every spec change is a new version. A revision runs as a job and is applied only to the version it was written for. Merged in pull request #33.

phases.title: Board and New episode screens
phases.note: The Board shows the episodes in the groups of the mockups, with loading, empty and error states, and New episode starts one from an idea. Merged in pull request #34.

phases.title: Episode workspace with Plan tab and revise flow
phases.note: The episode workspace: pipeline, tabs, the Plan tab with brief, claims, duration bar and scene cards that are edited in place, raw JSON, a change asked for in words with its diff, and the gate bar. In review as a pull request.

wins.text: An idea becomes an approved plan in the browser: type it, read the plan, ask for a change in words, apply it, approve. Tested on a 390 px screen through the real API and worker.
The first working screens: New episode takes an idea on a phone or a desktop, and the Board shows it move to Needs you with Approve the plan.
The planning flow works through the API in the running stack: an idea is created, reaches the plan gate by itself, is revised in words, shown as a diff, applied and approved.

All seven planner skills ran live in a row on the owner's plan: one idea became a brief, research, a script, a directed spec the theme can draw, a picture plan and an upload package in under two minutes.
The planner can think: an idea becomes a brief, checked facts and a script that fits its length, with one corrective retry and every claim tied to a page that was really retrieved.
First live calls: from the worker container through the bridge to Claude Code and Codex on the owner's plans, at no cost, with the pages of a web search coming back as sources.

The app now knows when to hold back: it counts its own use of each plan, pauses at the owner's budget, waits out a usage limit until the reset time, and checks the providers without spending anything on healthy ones.

Subscription mode is wired end to end in code: the planner asks Claude Code and the second reviewer asks Codex through the host bridge, covered by the owner's plans, and a usage limit pauses the job instead of ever reaching a paid API.

Subscription mode has its bridge: a small service on the PC that runs the Claude Code and Codex command line tools for the worker and refuses any sign-in that is billed per use. Checked from a container, and every flag checked against the installed tools without a model call.
The project has its public home on GitHub: 21 cards merged as pull requests, CI green on main, main protected, and the first container images published.

The pipeline can talk to a language model: recorded answers in demo mode, Claude through the API when the owner switches it on, with cost recorded per call and the key proven absent from every log line.
The paid API guard is in place before any paid adapter exists: no mode switch, no fallback, and a paid call cannot be recorded as anything else.
Episodes can move: the pipeline runs from an idea to the plan gate by itself, waits for approval, takes a rejection with a comment, and after an edit makes only the stale scenes again.

Milestone M1 works end to end on this PC: make demo-render turns the sample spec into a correct 44 second video with voice, music and sound cues inside the worker image, in 53 seconds. It needs no keys, no GPU and no downloads.

A resolved spec now becomes a real video file: scenes encoded on their own, joined frame-exact with sound, and a change to one scene re-encodes only that scene. The 23 second test episode renders in 27 seconds.
The video has sound: narration, sound cues and an original music bed that steps back under the voice, mixed to -14 LUFS. FFmpeg's own meter confirms the numbers.
The voice works: the real Kokoro model speaks a scene inside the worker image, with a pronunciation dictionary and word timings that follow the pauses in the audio. No GPL package is a dependency.

The compositor draws every scene kind and primitive: slam text, word-by-word captions, scroll unroll, pinned tags, stamps, smoke, clips. The same spec gives the same frames, checked by 14 golden frames.
The night_scrolls theme exists: original artwork and sounds drawn by code, bundled OFL fonts, and a capabilities list the planner cannot step outside.
Resolver done: an authored spec plus voice timings becomes a resolved spec with absolute times, and a video more than 2 seconds off target says which scenes to change.
M1 started: JSON Schemas for all six pipeline documents, with 88 fixtures that validate or fail exactly where they say.
Architecture document and six decision records written, with a test that fails when the pipeline diagram and the code disagree, and a test that enforces the package boundaries.
Delivery is ready to switch on: release and nightly workflows, weekly Dependabot updates, a release Compose file and a script for branch protection.
CI workflow with all ten required jobs is written, linted and each job command passes locally, including the 80 percent coverage gate and a secret scan that catches a planted token.
The app shell is up: sidebar on desktop, icon rail on tablet, bottom bar on a phone, a status strip fed by /health and an empty Board, checked by 28 browser tests.
API skeleton: /health reports database, storage, ComfyUI and demo mode, every error has one shape, and the typed web client is generated with drift checks.
Job queue and worker: a no-op job completes in the real stack, two workers never take the same job, one gpu job at a time, and jobs survive worker and database restarts.
Database baseline: 15 tables migrate up and down cleanly on real Postgres, and models and migration agree.
docker compose up brings web, api, worker and db to healthy, with every port bound to 127.0.0.1 and containers reaching the host.
Progress tracker in place: this page, its JSON twin and a local server with live git state, kept in sync by a test and a pre-commit hook.
Repository skeleton verified on a fresh clone: setup, every pre-commit hook and all checks pass.
Asset licence check written test-first: a sample file without a registry row fails the build.
